title: EXP-040 — Hello World Part 1: Single-Wizard FX_ SQL Table and IDO Creation
objective: Determine whether the authenticated Site Developer user, working in the intended DEM configuration with Designer editing scope User, can use the supported Runtime Builder DataMaintenance wizard to generate exactly one SQL table and one IDO from the shared requested name FX_HelloWorld01, associated with the existing IDO project FX_HelloWorldProject01. Define exactly two application string fields, FX_Code with length 30 and FX_Label with length 100. Inspect and record wizard defaults, resulting object names, and the complete creation scope before committing through one Finish action. Decline any optional Form generation. Verify the resulting SQL table, columns, IDO, base-table association, properties, and check-out state through supported maintenance forms. If the newly generated FX_HelloWorld01 IDO requires check-in, perform at most one supported check-in of that IDO only. Close and reopen the clean verification surfaces and confirm the same metadata is recoverable. Classify findings as observed at UI level only.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, EXP-001, EXP-002, EXP-038, EXP-039, environments/current-environment.md, docs/mongoose/guides/ido-development.md, and the relevant Hello World Part 1 transcript before browser mutation.
Confirm the authenticated DEM configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT and inspect the available Site Developer permission evidence.

Use the supported Web Client Designer launch route and Identify Your Editing Scope dialog with User selected. Record that User editing scope does not necessarily isolate SQL tables or IDOs from other users of the configuration.
Verify that FX_HelloWorldProject01 exists exactly once in IDO Projects, with its expected description and displayed Access As G6R, and that its maintenance record is clean.

Establish working, positive-control queries in SQL Tables and IDOs before interpreting target-name absence. Confirm zero exact and case-insensitive collisions for FX_HelloWorld01 through supported visible evidence. Stop before mutation if the relevant inventory or query cannot be trusted.
Use the documented Designer and Runtime Builder Selection workflow: Category FormBuilder, Runtime Builder DataMaintenance, then Data Maintenance Wizard.
Inspect each accessible wizard page and record field labels, available controls, defaults, mandatory entries, naming requirements, and displayed creation effects before advancing beyond that page.
Enter IDO Name exactly FX_HelloWorld01.
Replace the wizard's default IDO Project Name HelloWorld with the existing FX_HelloWorldProject01. Verify the replacement before Finish.
Record the Table Alias default exactly as displayed. Retain a supported default unless the wizard explicitly requires a different value; stop rather than invent an unsupported alias.
Inspect and clear the applicable Multi-Site options. Record their exact visible labels and final unchecked state.

Configure exactly two user-defined application fields in the wizard: FX_Code as a string of length 30, and FX_Label as a string of length 100. Record type, length, and any mandatory or key-related settings.
Allow only necessary automatically generated system columns or identifiers. Record them separately from the two requested application fields.
Inspect and record the Form Type, Layout, and Device Type defaults without changing them.

Before Finish, inspect any available summary or final wizard page showing the intended SQL table, IDO, and other generated objects. Stop if the intended creation scope cannot be determined sufficiently to protect the FX_ naming boundary.

Record any automatically derived physical table name, including a generated suffix or tenant qualification. A tenant-generated qualification is acceptable only when the underlying custom identifier is unambiguously FX_HelloWorld01 and no independently named non-FX_ custom object is being introduced.
After all prerequisites pass, invoke the supported wizard Finish action at most once.
Inspect the completion result and record whether the wizard reports successful SQL table and IDO generation, a partial result, validation failure, or an uncertain result.
Decline any optional Create Form prompt using its supported negative choice. Capture the prompt and resulting state.

Open SQL Tables through its supported maintenance form, find the generated table by its actual name, and record its definition, user-defined columns, types, lengths, and automatically generated system columns.

Open IDOs or IDO Projects through supported maintenance forms and confirm that FX_HelloWorld01 belongs to FX_HelloWorldProject01. Inspect its displayed base-table association and property definitions.

Inspect the newly generated FX_HelloWorld01 IDO's check-out state. If it is checked out and the supported check-in can be confined to FX_HelloWorld01, perform at most one ordinary check-in and capture the outcome.
Inspect any supported Save requirement associated with the generated objects, allowing at most one ordinary Save on an explicitly dirty FX_ target record and no retry of an uncertain commit.
After clean verification, close the SQL Tables and IDO maintenance surfaces normally, reopen each through supported navigation, and query the target definitions again.

Capture decisive screenshots, accessibility snapshots, and supported response evidence under evidence/EXP-040/ for the wizard configuration, Finish outcome, resulting table, IDO, check-out or check-in state, and post-reopen metadata.
Record all user-created and visible system-generated artifacts, exact object names, operation counts, errors, recovery usage, and unexpected side effects.
Update only the EXP-040 experiment record and evidence/EXP-040/. Keep Playwright MCP automatically generated, Git-ignored output separate from intentional repository changes.
out_of_scope: Creating a Mongoose Form, including a Data Maintenance Form, even if the wizard offers one.
Creating any application data rows or performing runtime CRUD tests.
Adding more than the two specified application fields.
Adding custom events, scripts, workflows, business logic, relationships, or calculated properties.
Using Get Database Schema or importing an existing database schema.
Creating a second SQL table or a second IDO through another creation path.
Creating another IDO project or changing FX_HelloWorldProject01 settings other than its intended membership in the generated IDO.
Changing any non-FX_ SQL table, IDO, project, Form, or other Mongoose artifact.
Changing Access As G6R or inventing an alternate Access As identifier.
Direct SQL execution, direct database access, unsupported endpoints, or browser-injected code.
FormSync, explicit metadata-cache operations, regeneration, or deployment.
Launching an alternative wizard after the designated wizard fails.
Testing database durability, server-session independence, cache eviction, or behavior for other users.
Automatically deleting or rolling back any generated object.
Starting EXP-041 or any unrelated experiment.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Never create, modify, or delete a user-controlled Mongoose artifact whose name does not begin with FX_.
Never rename the requested IDO from FX_HelloWorld01 or substitute another IDO project.
Never proceed if FX_HelloWorld01 already exists as an IDO or conflicts with the intended SQL table, or if the collision assessment remains inconclusive.
Never proceed if the existing project FX_HelloWorldProject01 cannot be positively identified and selected.
Never modify the existing project's Description, Access As, security settings, or unrelated membership.
Never manually override the displayed Access As G6R.
Never invoke Get Database Schema.
Never leave an applicable Multi-Site option selected at Finish.
Never add extra application fields or change the requested string lengths.
Never invoke Finish until the wizard's intended effects, supported naming, fields, and project association have been inspected.
Never press Finish more than once or retry after an uncertain completion.
Never press a positive Create Form confirmation. If the prompt cannot be safely declined, stop.
Never continue to another creation wizard after a wizard-loading, validation, permission, or Finish failure.
Never assume the SQL table has the same physical name as the IDO; read the actual displayed identifier.
Never accept an unrelated non-FX_ custom table name or generated custom artifact as an authorized side effect.
Never change any existing SQL table or IDO while querying the inventory or inspecting the target.
Never check in or check out a non-FX_ IDO, an entire project, or multiple IDOs.
Never perform more than one check-in of FX_HelloWorld01, and never repeat a check-in with an uncertain outcome.
Never retry an uncertain Save or create operation.
Never add application records to the newly generated table.
Never execute direct SQL or database maintenance commands.
Never bypass permission failures or disabled UI controls through scripts, unsupported APIs, or hidden controls.
Never deliberately sign in, reauthenticate, reset the browser session, or restart services during the experiment. Stop if authentication is required.
Never perform FormSync, metadata-cache unloading, regeneration, deployment, or synchronization.
Never delete any generated object without separate operator authorization.
Never exceed one fresh recovery snapshot and one corrected visible inspection after an inspection failure.
Never change repository files outside the EXP-040 experiment record and evidence/EXP-040/.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence identifies the documented Data Maintenance wizard procedure, AGENTS.md authorization, EXP-038 limitation, EXP-039 accepted project, intended DEM configuration, authenticated UI, Site Developer evidence where available, and User editing scope. It explicitly states that SQL table and IDO visibility may be configuration-wide. A settled screenshot or snapshot identifies the intended environment and maintenance controls.

Before mutation, a supported positive-control lookup proves the relevant SQL Tables and IDO query mechanism. Saved screenshots or accessibility snapshots show zero exact and case-insensitive collisions for FX_HelloWorld01 and exactly one existing FX_HelloWorldProject01 project with the expected Description and Access As G6R. The evidence states any inventory-completeness limitation.

The supported Designer and Runtime Builder workflow visibly opens the Data Maintenance Wizard with Category FormBuilder and Runtime Builder DataMaintenance. Evidence shows the required UI was reached without an authentication or wizard-loading error. A ComponentFlags or similar wizard error fails this check and stops mutation.

Pre-Finish evidence visibly identifies IDO Name FX_HelloWorld01, IDO Project Name FX_HelloWorldProject01, the exact Table Alias default or documented required value, cleared Multi-Site options, and the recorded Form Type, Layout, and Device Type defaults. No unsupported value or unexpected generated-object requirement remains unresolved before Finish.

The wizard field grid visibly contains exactly two requested application string fields: FX_Code length 30 and FX_Label length 100. Evidence distinguishes these from any automatically generated system fields. The field definitions remain unchanged immediately before Finish.

A supported pre-Finish inspection identifies the intended SQL table and IDO generation scope. Exactly one Finish action is performed. A completion message, rendered resulting object state, or supported captured response identifies the outcome. No second Finish, alternative creation wizard, or unrelated creation operation is performed. A partial or uncertain result is recorded without retry.

Any optional Create Form prompt is visibly declined, and the final supported Form inventory or control-verified lookup confirms that no Form named FX_HelloWorld01 was generated. Evidence shows that no application data rows were intentionally inserted.

The SQL Tables maintenance form retrieves the newly generated table using its exact actual identifier. Evidence identifies the table and shows FX_Code as string length 30 and FX_Label as string length 100, with any generated system columns recorded separately. A physically different name is recorded as a naming finding, provided the custom FX_ identity and naming boundary remain satisfied.

IDO Projects or IDOs retrieves exactly one FX_HelloWorld01 IDO associated with FX_HelloWorldProject01. The displayed base table matches the actual generated SQL table. The IDO properties corresponding to FX_Code and FX_Label are identifiable in supported rendered evidence. No unrelated IDO or project record was altered.

The IDO's initial check-out state is captured. If it is checked out, evidence shows no more than one supported check-in applied to FX_HelloWorld01 only, followed by the resulting settled check-out state. If already checked in, evidence establishes that no check-in was attempted. Any Save or check-in failure stops further mutation without retry.

After clean verification, the SQL Tables and IDO maintenance surfaces are ordinarily closed and reopened through supported controls. Fresh queries retrieve the same table, both application columns with matching types and lengths, and the same IDO, base-table association, properties, and project membership. The recovered surfaces show no pending changes or validation errors. Findings are limited to observed UI-level recovery.

The final evidence matrix maps AC-1 through AC-11 to exact existing screenshots, accessibility snapshots, or supported captured-response files under evidence/EXP-040/. The object audit lists the actual table name, IDO, application fields, any visible system-generated dependencies, and any unverified effects. The operation audit reconciles Finish, Save, check-in, close, reopen, query, errors, and recovery counts. Repository changes are confined to the EXP-040 record and evidence/EXP-040/. No database-durability, cross-session, replay-verification, or cache-behavior claim is made.

initial_instruction: T1 — Repository review and read-only preflight only. Read AGENTS.md, EXP-001, EXP-002, EXP-038, EXP-039, the current-environment record, the local IDO development guide, and the Hello World Part 1 transcript covering the Data Maintenance wizard. Inspect the inherited browser state without authentication or mutation. Confirm the intended DEM configuration and available Designer access, note the current editing scope, and inspect the existing IDO Projects surface. Use supported rendered controls to identify FX_HelloWorldProject01 and determine whether the SQL Tables and IDOs inventory can support reliable positive-control and target-collision checks. Capture the initial UI and prerequisite evidence under evidence/EXP-040/. Document any wizard-navigation prerequisites and possible configuration-wide effects. Stop before launching the creation wizard, entering wizard values, pressing Finish, saving, or checking anything in or out. Report whether the experiment can safely proceed to the separately authorized wizard-inspection task. Preserve the existing project and all unrelated objects.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-111209-OE9H. Rationale: EXP-039 established that the current user can create, save, close, reopen, and recover the FX_HelloWorldProject01 IDO project. EXP-038 was blocked before mutation while examining the separate SQL Tables and IDOs maintenance approach. EXP-040 tests a different, tutorial-documented path: the New Data Maintenance wizard, which is intended to generate the SQL table and IDO together. The experiment treats that paired generation as one controlled wizard operation, limits custom object names to the FX_ namespace, and verifies each resulting definition independently. It does not replay EXP-038 or assume that its blocked procedure is usable. | Operator review: exact-value and no-JavaScript guards added; the create-form pattern now ignores mentions of the wizard's Create Form prompt so an instruction to decline it is not flagged; EXP-036-R2 added to related experiments. Standard lessons apply: the Designer may open in its own tab (select a tab before acting on it, then take a fresh snapshot); ExtJS checkboxes toggle via their visible label; comboboxes take a literal value plus Enter; one browser action at a time. Approved by the operator 2026-10-10.
